learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the true meaning of Democracy, its key features, and why it is widely considered the best form of government in the modern world!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Derived from Greek words 'Demos' (people) and 'Kratos' (rule). As Abraham Lincoln said, it is a government 'of the people, by the people, and for the people.'
Final decision-making power rests with elected representatives. It features free and fair elections, 'One Person, One Vote, One Value', and the rule of law protecting citizen rights.
Direct: Citizens vote on laws directly (e.g., ancient Athens, modern Switzerland). Indirect (Representative): Citizens elect leaders to make laws on their behalf (e.g., India, USA).
It is an accountable form of government, improves the quality of decision-making (through consultation), provides a method to resolve conflicts peacefully, and enhances the dignity of citizens.
Leaders keep changing, causing instability. Decision-making can be slow because many people must be consulted. Electoral competition can sometimes lead to corruption.

fun_activity.title: 🗳️ Class Election
fun_activity.instructions: If your class was a democracy, what is the first rule you would vote to change? Remember, in a democracy, the majority wins, but the minority's rights must still be protected!

exam_tips: 📌 Always memorize Abraham Lincoln's definition of democracy—it is perfect for starting any long-answer question.
📌 Be able to explain 'One Person, One Vote, One Value'. (It means everyone's vote has equal weight, whether rich or poor).
📌 Questions asking you to compare Democracy with Dictatorship are very common. Focus on accountability and civil rights.
quick_recap: ⭐ Democracy ensures that the rulers are accountable to the people.
⭐ A democratic government rules within limits set by constitutional law and citizens' rights.
⭐ Even though democracy has flaws, it is considered the best alternative because it allows us to correct our own mistakes.
